outcome: Need for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
cohort: Singleton pregnancies in adolescents (maternal age <19 years) compared to young adults (maternal age 20 years)
finding: Neonatal problems and poor obstetric outcomes are more common in adolescent pregnancies compared to young adults, highlighting the need for family planning and baby care social training.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in the group of mothers aged 20 years or older.
